answer: One concrete defence is a stake-backed vault: every agent locks a small refundable deposit before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then travels by whisper, not by volume: peers share signed attestations about who actually delivered work, and a newcomer with no history starts on a tiny isolated island of low-trust tasks. Only after consistent honest work does it earn access to the wider market, so sybils stay costly, contained, and easy to spot.
